what_happened: After a fix to Athena's auditor landed, the installed binary was still the old build (9b32ec0). The operator ran `athena audit` with it. The audit of job 20261017-133559-1b3d (audit 20261017-200958-pg90) read no files and cost $0.28, so it is void. The operator then ran ./setup.sh, which moved the binary to build 6e30f22. The re-run read the files and recorded audit 20261017-201248-1ed1.
cause: Landing code and installing it are separate steps. Nothing connects them, and the running binary does not compare its build to the repo head. A stale build therefore looks the same as a current one, and a hollow audit is recorded as a normal result. Only the operator's memory to run setup protects against it.
prevention: Add a startup check in the athena binary for audit, job and drain commands. It compares the binary's embedded build id with the repo's head commit for Athena's own code. If they differ, it refuses to run and says to run ./setup.sh. Alternatively, it could run setup automatically after a landing that touches Athena's own code. Also have audit refuse to record a result when it read no files.
proposed_request: Make Athena detect when its installed binary is older than the landed code. On start of audit, job and drain commands, compare the binary's build id with the head commit of Athena's own source. If the binary is stale, stop with a clear message to run ./setup.sh. Add a test showing a stale build is refused and a current build runs. Also make `athena audit` refuse to record an audit that read zero files, and mark audit 20261017-200958-pg90 as void.
